exercise.name: Cable Front Raise
library_steps: Stand facing away from a low pulley with a rope running between your legs.
Raise your hands straight out in front up to shoulder height.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing with the back to a low pulley, a rope running between the legs and held in both fists; straight arms rise from the thighs to shoulder height in front. Front delt does the work; the upper chest helps.

setup.target: Low pulley behind; the rope/cable runs between the legs.
Feet a little wider than hips.
setup.why: Lets the cable pass between the legs.

movement.measure: arm raised forward from hanging, 0 = down

muscles.emg: The frontal raise mainly works the front delt (S1); front delt active in raises (S2).
muscles.role: Lifts the arm forward; what the exercise is for.

muscles.emg: Pectoralis major higher in the frontal raise than in any lateral raise (S1).
muscles.role: Helps lift the arm forward; library secondary.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Leaning back to heave the rope up.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The shoulders should lift the load.

sources.citation: Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Esposito F, Ce E. 2020. An electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015.
sources.what_it_gave: Lateral raise variants vs frontal raise: frontal raise mainly works the front delt (with pectoralis major more than any lateral raise); lateral raise with a neutral humerus works the side delt most; internal rotation shifts work to the rear delt and upper trapezius.

sources.citation: Campos YAC, Vianna JM, Guimaraes MP, et al. 2020. Different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals. J Hum Kinet 75:5-14.
sources.what_it_gave: Bench press, dumbbell fly, shoulder press, lateral raise at 60 % 1RM: front delt only ~19 % MVIC in the fly; side delt highest in the lateral raise (30 %).

clip_check.check: Start: hands in front of the thighs
End: straight arms at shoulder height
Both fists closed on the rope; cable runs back between the legs, clear of them
Front delts strongest red, upper chest light
